Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Place: a city park with benches, old trees and a fountain
Time of day: golden hour — warm low sun, long shadows; the warm low sun rim-lighting her hair.
Light direction: dappled light — patches of light with leaf or blind shadow across her.
Outfit: a fitted navy police-style party costume with a short-brimmed cap and a short-sleeved button shirt, no real insignia, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.

COMPOSITION: a waist-up shot of her head, torso and hands; body facing the camera; camera at her eye level; she is placed in the right third of the frame, open space of the place to her left.
Lens / perspective: 50mm-equivalent natural perspective with balanced proportions and modest depth compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand reaches gently toward the camera.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand rests lightly on her collarbone.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: brows released upward and outward, eyes half closed, breath-out mouth slightly open, whole face loosened.

Framing: a waist-up shot — the bottom edge crosses her waist; hips, legs and feet are out of frame.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — actinium: a soft silvery-white metal named from the Greek for a ray or beam, found in 1899 in the residues of pitchblende ore and again in 1902 by a chemist at a quinine works; its own radiation wakes the surrounding air so that it glows a pale blue in the dark, and gram for gram it is some hundred and fifty times more radioactive than radium; the fifteen elements from actinium to lawrencium, uranium and plutonium among them, are called the actinides after it; born from protactinium, it now and then gives rise to francium, and one short-lived form is being made into an alpha-ray medicine that strikes only cancer cells — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Figure: keep her exact build from the attached image, neither slimmer nor fuller.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
